To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the production of the ribosomally-synthesized, post-translation modification peptide antibiotic trifolitoxin by the avirulent A. vitis strain F2/5 confers biological control of crown gall disease on N. glauca.

(1) the production of the peptide antibiotic trifolitoxin (by an avirulent Agrobacterium strain) confers biological control of Agrobacterum-induced crown gall disease in Nicotiana glanica, (2) this biological control is most effective at a 10-fold ratio of the avirulent to the tumorigenic strain, (3) this biological control activity is not improved by a 24 h pre-treatment with trifolitoxin, and (
TFX production by a non-tumorigenic strain of Agrobacteria vitis confers biological control of crown gall disease on tobacco.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an avirulent Agrobacterium strain that produces trifolitoxin and is capable of controlling crown gall disease on grape.
the development of biological control of crown gall disease by using an avirulent, genetically engineered strain of A. tumefaciens.
the development of biological control strategies to reduce the incidence and severity of crown gall disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of the TFX production and resistance genes to an avirulant strain of A. viits does confer biological control of crown gall disease on N. glauca.

the production of TFX by a non-pathogenic Agrobacterium strain can be used to reduce the incidence of crown gall disease on N. glauca, a model plant host, but the level of control achieved is strain-dependent and may be influenced by environmental conditions.
the production of TFX by an avirultent A. vitis strain confers biological control activity against A. vitis on Nicotiana plants.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the production of TFX can confer biological control to an avirultent strain of A. viis.
we have demonstrated that TFX production can be used to control crown gall in N. glauca, but the efficacy is dependent on the ratio of the TFX producing strain to tumorigenic Agrobacterium.

the production of the TFX by a non-pathogenic strain of Agrobacteria, such as F2/5 (pT2TFXk), is effective in controlling crown gall disease in a plant host, but only at high ratios of the TFX producing strain to the pathogenic strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of TFX by the avirulent strain, F2/5 can be used as an alternative to the biological control of crown gall disease in the vineyard.
the production of an antimicrobial agent by an avirultent strain of a pathogen can reduce plant disease caused by that pathogen.
the production of TFX by an avirultent strain of Agrobactetium can be used to reduce disease incidence caused by a virulent strain of Ag. vitis.
